title: Nepal demands £15m climate compensation from ‘polluting economies’ - Yahoo
description: Nepal demands £15m climate compensation from ‘polluting economies’  Yahoo
publisher.title: Yahoo
full_article:
Nepal has demanded £15m in climate compensation from "polluting economies" for last month's devastating flood.

At least 1,399 people have been confirmed dead and more than 5,500 remain missing on the 12th day of rescue operations.

Shisir Khanal, Nepal's foreign minister, said the country had requested climate compensation from the UN.

The money will come from the UN's fund for responding to loss and damage, set up in 2022 in line with the Paris climate agreement.

"We have contributed so little to climate change," Mr Khanal told The Guardian.

The rescue and recovery effort has been complicated by the destruction of more than 40 bridges - Getty Images/Pedro Pardo

He added: "It is imperative for those in the global community who benefit from larger, much more polluting economies, and whose historical contribution to greenhouse gases is much bigger than ours, to accept a shared responsibility.

"This affects all of humanity. The global community should not see this as a one-off disaster. It should be viewed in the context of the changing climate in the Himalayas.

"We know it is going to be a recurring scenario that more and more communities, not just in Nepal but around the world, will have to face."

Mr Khanal said India and China should step in to help, but did not mention the US, the world's second-biggest polluter.

The UN climate fund, which has so far received $820m (£600m) in pledges, has been held back by wealthy nations that have been reluctant to contribute.

The US promised $17.5m under Joe Biden but exited the fund under Donald Trump.

Damaged and mud-covered houses in Nuwakot, pictured on Sunday as rescue efforts continued - Getty Images/Pedro Pardo

Both China and Nepal have blamed climate change for the glacier collapse that triggered the flood on Aug 26, sweeping through both countries.

Nepal contributes 0.04 per cent of the world's CO2 emissions, compared to neighbouring India and China, two of the world's largest emitters at 33.1 per cent and 8 per cent respectively.

Mr Khanal said the compensation Nepal had requested from the UN was "obviously not nearly enough" to repair the damage caused by the floods. The total cost has been estimated at $5bn.

However, Mr Khanal said the true cost could be even higher as entire villages would have to be rebuilt.

A national day of mourning in Kathmandu. The death toll has reached 1,399, with 5,500 missing - Getty Images/Prakash Mathema

Twelve days after the floods, rescue efforts are continuing, as experts warn the possibility of finding missing people alive is diminishing.

On Saturday, a Chinese man was rescued from a 225m hydropower tunnel in the Upper Trishuli-1 hydropower project, and two Nepali workers were rescued from another tunnel on Friday.

A 64-year-old Nepali woman was rescued from a damaged house in the town of Nuwakot, days after the floods.

Rescue efforts have been complicated by the damage caused by the disaster, with more than 40 bridges having collapsed.

full_article:
Pope Leo XIV expressed his deep sorrow and spiritual closeness to people affected by tragedies in Indonesia, Zimbabwe, and Nepal during the month of August.

In a telegram addressed to Archbishop Paulus Budi Kleden, SVD, of Ende, the Holy Father expressed his “spiritual solidarity and closeness to those suffering the continuing effects” of the 7.7-magnitude earthquake that struck the Region of East Nusa Tenggara, Indonesia, on Saturday morning, 15 August, killing at least 1oo people, injuring over 1,500 and leaving thousands homeless.

The Pope also encouraged the ecclesial and civil authorities as they continued to provide humanitarian assistance and ensured his prayers “for the emergency personnel engaged in recovery efforts”.

On Tuesday, 18 August, in a telegram signed by Secretary of State Cardinal Pietro Parolin, the Holy Father expressed his grief for the victims of the ferry disaster in Zimbabwe, and prayed for all affected by the tragedy.

The accident claimed the lives of more than 90 people, including numerous children. In the telegram, the Pope expressed his “heartfelt condolences” to the bereaved, and offered his prayers for the Civil Authorities and emergency personnel who responded to the tragedy. He entrusted the souls of those who died “to the loving mercy of Almighty God”; and invoked “the Divine Blessings of consolation, healing and strength”.

On Thursday, 27 August, the Pope expressed his sadness over the loss of life and widespread devastation caused by flash floods in Nepal. The Pope assured all those affected by the disaster of his “spiritual closeness” and prayed for the “emergency personnel engaged in the ongoing rescue efforts”. The telegram concluded with the Pope’s prayers for God’s assistance and protection upon the people of Nepal.

More than 1,250 people have died in Nepal, while thousands remain unaccounted for after a devastating torrent of water, mud and debris swept through communities near the country’s northern border with China. Hundreds more are missing in neighbouring Tibet, bringing the total number of people unaccounted for across the affected region to almost 1,500.

The Vatican announced that Pope Leo, through the Dicastery for the Service of Charity, had sent financial assistance to Caritas Nepal to help meet the most urgent needs of people affected by the disaster.

एन्डे केरऽ आर्कबिशप पौलस बुडी क्लेडन, एसवीडी क॑ संबोधित एगो तार म॑ पवित्र पिता न॑ इंडोनेशिया केरऽ पूर्वी नुसा टेंगारा क्षेत्र म॑ शनिदिन सुबह १५ अगस्त क॑ ७.७ तीव्रता के भूकंप केरऽ “आध्यात्मिक एकजुटता आरू लगातार प्रभाव स॑ ग्रस्त लोगऽ के साथ निकटता” व्यक्त करलकै, जेकरा म॑ कम स॑ कम १oo लोगऽ के मौत होय गेलै, जेकरा म॑ १,५०० आरू घायल होय गेलै हजारों बेघर छोड़कर।

पोप न॑ चर्च आरू नागरिक अधिकारियऽ क॑ भी प्रोत्साहित करलकै, कैन्हेंकि हुनी मानवीय सहायता जारी रखलकै आरू हुनकऽ प्रार्थना सुनिश्चित करलकै कि “वसूली के प्रयास म॑ जुटलऽ आपातकालीन कर्मी सिनी लेली” ।

मंगलवार, 18 अगस्त क॑ विदेश सचिव कार्डिनल पिएट्रो पैरोलिन केरऽ हस्ताक्षर वाला तार म॑ पवित्र पिता न॑ जिम्बाब्वे म॑ फेरी आपदा के शिकार लोगऽ लेली अपनऽ दुख व्यक्त करलकै, आरू ई त्रासदी स॑ प्रभावित सब लोगऽ लेली प्रार्थना करलकै ।

एहि दुर्घटना मे 90 स बेसी लोक क जान गेल, जाहि मे कईटा बच्चा सेहो शामिल अछि। तार म॑ पोप न॑ शोक संतप्त लोगऽ के प्रति अपनऽ “हृदय संवेदना” व्यक्त करलकै, आरू ई त्रासदी के प्रतिक्रिया दै वाला नागरिक प्राधिकरण आरू आपातकालीन कर्मी लेली अपनऽ प्रार्थना करलकै । ओ मरल लोकक आत्मा केँ “सर्वशक्तिमान परमेश् वरक प्रेमपूर्ण दया” सौंपलनि; आ “सांत्वना, चिकित्सा आ बल के दिव्य आशीर्वाद” के आह्वान केलक |

गुरुवार, 27 अगस्त क॑ पोप न॑ नेपाल म॑ आकस्मिक बाढ़ स॑ होय वाला जानमाल के नुकसान आरू व्यापक तबाही प॑ दुख व्यक्त करलकै । पोप न॑ आपदा स॑ प्रभावित सब लोगऽ क॑ अपनऽ “आध्यात्मिक निकटता” के आश्वासन देलकै आरू “चलै वाला बचाव प्रयास म॑ जुटलऽ आपातकालीन कर्मी” लेली प्रार्थना करलकै । तार केरऽ समापन पोप केरऽ नेपाल केरऽ जनता प॑ भगवान केरऽ सहायता आरू सुरक्षा केरऽ प्रार्थना स॑ करलऽ गेलै ।

नेपाल मे 1250 स बेसी लोक के मौत भ चुकल अछि, जखन कि चीन के संग देश के उत्तरी सीमा के पास समुदाय मे पानि, थाल आ मलबा के विनाशकारी धार बहला के बाद हजारों लोक के कोनो हिसाब नहिं अछि. पड़ोसी देश तिब्बत म॑ सैकड़ों आरू लोगऽ के लापता छै, जेकरा स॑ पूरा प्रभावित क्षेत्र म॑ बेहिसाब लोगऽ के संख्या लगभग १५०० होय गेलऽ छै ।

वेटिकन न॑ घोषणा करलकै कि पोप लियो न॑ डिकास्ट्री फॉर द सर्विस ऑफ चैरिटी के माध्यम स॑ कैरिटास नेपाल क॑ आर्थिक सहायता भेजलकै ताकि आपदा स॑ प्रभावित लोगऽ के सबसें जरूरी जरूरत पूरा करै म॑ मदद मिल॑ सक॑ ।

full_article:
In brief SBS News understands an Australian citizen who was in Nepal has confirmed they are safe.

Thousands of people, including 35 Australians, are still unaccounted for.

An Australian citizen who was in Nepal has been confirmed safe in the wake of the catastrophic flooding that swept through the region nearly two weeks ago.

The Australian was uncontactable but has today confirmed they are safe and well and do not require consular assistance, SBS News understands.

There are still 35 Australians who remain unaccounted for in the region.

SKIP ADVERTISEMENT

At least 1,399 people were killed by the 26 August mudslide and flooding in Nepal and Tibet and more than 5,400 are missing, including around 800 foreigners.

A group of Australian families with missing loved ones released a statement on Sunday, calling for greater transparency from tour groups and authorities.

They expressed gratitude to the Australian Federal Police and search teams working to find missing Australians, but criticised the Australian government for what they said was its failure to provide answers.

The federal government has sent a disaster assistance response team and other specialist resources to Kathmandu to assist with the search.

It has also committed $11 million to support the disaster response, which Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said on Monday was of national importance.

Race to find hydropower workers

Hundreds of hydropower workers are among the missing, but the rescue of three of them from deep inside tunnels — two Nepalis on Friday and a Chinese man on Saturday — have buoyed hopes that more could still be alive.

At least 11 hydropower projects were engulfed when a glacier collapsed into a river on the Nepal-China border on August 26, burying the entrances to the tunnels of these projects under debris and mud and cutting off those trapped inside.

READ MORE 'We have a lot of hope': Nepal holds national day of mourning as 36 Australians still missing

Authorities said Tuesday that rescuers in Nepal are focusing on three hydropower project tunnels where they believe dozens of workers could be trapped.

"Our search operation is focussed on finding survivors, including in tunnels. Our bigger focus is on the Chilime hydroelectric project, where we believe people are trapped, because there was a canteen, residency and arrangements for food," Dharma Raj Upreti, chief of the country's disaster authority, told Reuters.

Australian tunnel rescue expert Arnold Dix, who is advising Nepali teams, has said the operation presents an unprecedented challenge.

"We are facing something I have never faced before," he said earlier this week.

"Not one rescue, but multiple potential rescues, unfolding at the same time, in different places, each with its own dangers, uncertainties, and lives that may still be saved."

— With additional reporting by AAP, Reuters and Agence France-Presse

35 ऑस्ट्रेलियाई सहित हजारों लोक के एखन धरि कोनो हिसाब नहिं अछि.

लगभग दू सप्ताह पहिने एहि क्षेत्र मे आयल भयावह बाढ़ि के बाद नेपाल मे रहल एकटा ऑस्ट्रेलियाई नागरिक के सुरक्षित पुष्टि भेल अछि ।

एसबीएस न्यूज के समझ में आबै छै कि ऑस्ट्रेलियाई ई खिलाड़ी संपर्क नै कर॑ सकै छेलै लेकिन आय ई बात के पुष्टि करी देल॑ छै कि हुनी सुरक्षित आरू ठीक छै आरू ओकरा कांसुलर सहायता के जरूरत नै छै ।

विज्ञापन छोड़ि दियौक

नेपाल आ तिब्बत मे 26 अगस्त के भेल कीचड़ आ बाढ़ि मे कम सं कम 1399 लोक के मौत भ गेल अछि आओर करीब 800 विदेशी सहित 5400 सं बेसि लोक लापता अछि.

लापता प्रियजन वाला ऑस्ट्रेलियाई परिवारऽ के एगो समूह न॑ रविवार क॑ एगो बयान जारी करी क॑ टूर ग्रुप आरू अधिकारियऽ स॑ अधिक पारदर्शिता के आह्वान करलकै ।

समाचार जे समझ मे आबै छै अपनऽ आसपास के दुनिया स॑ अपडेट रहै लेली आपने के विश्वसनीय स्रोत । मुफ्त में दैनिक समाचार अपडेट आ विश्लेषण प्राप्त करू, सीधा अपन इनबॉक्स पर। ईमेल पता दर्ज करूं सदस्यता लें सुबह (सोम–शुक्र) दुपहर (सोम–शुक्र) सप्ताहांत अंतर्दृष्टि सदस्यता लेनाय सं, अहां एसबीएस सं ईमेल अपडेट प्राप्त करनाय सहित एसबीएस कें सेवा शर्तक आ गोपनीयता नीति सं सहमत छी.

हुनी लापता ऑस्ट्रेलियाई सिनी क खोजै मँ काम करै वाला ऑस्ट्रेलियाई संघीय पुलिस आरू खोज टीम के प्रति आभार व्यक्त करलकै, लेकिन ऑस्ट्रेलिया सरकार के आलोचना करलकै कि हुनी जे बात कहलकै कि हुनी जवाब नै दै छै ।

संघीय सरकार आपदा सहायता प्रतिक्रिया दल आ अन्य विशेषज्ञ संसाधन काठमांडू पठा क खोज मे सहयोग केने अछि ।

आपदा प्रतिक्रिया के समर्थन लेली भी एक करोड़ 10 लाख डॉलर के प्रतिबद्धता जतैन॑ छै, जेकरा प्रधानमंत्री एंथोनी अल्बानीज न॑ सोमवार क॑ कहलकै कि ई राष्ट्रीय महत्व के छै ।

जलविद्युत मजदूर खोजबाक दौड़

लापता मे सैकड़ों जलविद्युत मजदूर शामिल छथि, मुदा एहि मे स तीन गोटे कए गहींर भीतर सुरंग स बचाउल गेल – शुक्रदिन दूटा नेपाली आ शनिदिन एकटा चीनी मजदूर – एहि उम्मीद मे उछाल आबि गेल अछि जे एखनो आओर जीवित भ सकैत अछि।

26 अगस्त कए नेपाल-चीन सीमा पर एकटा ग्लेशियर नदी मे खसि पड़ला स कम स कम 11टा जलविद्युत परियोजना कए घेरि लेल गेल छल, जाहि स एहि परियोजना क सुरंग क प्रवेश द्वार मलबा आ थाल क नीचा गाड़ल गेल आ भीतर फंसल लोक कए काटि देल गेल।

देश केरऽ आपदा प्राधिकरण केरऽ प्रमुख धर्मराज उप्रेती न॑ रायटर क॑ बतैलकै कि हमरऽ खोज अभियान सुरंग सहित बची गेलऽ लोगऽ क॑ खोजै प॑ केंद्रित छै ।हमरऽ बड़ऽ ध्यान चिलीमे जलविद्युत परियोजना प॑ छै, जहां हमरा विश्वास छै कि लोग फंसलऽ छै, कैन्हेंकि वहाँ कैंटीन, निवास आरू भोजन के व्यवस्था छेलै ।

नेपाली टीम के सलाह देबय वाला ऑस्ट्रेलियाई सुरंग बचाव विशेषज्ञ अर्नोल्ड डिक्स के कहनाय छनि जे एहि अभियान के अभूतपूर्व चुनौती सामने आबि रहल अछि.

"एकटा बचाव नै, बल्कि अनेक संभावित बचाव, जे एकहि संग, अलग-अलग जगह पर खुलैत अछि, प्रत्येक के अपन-अपन खतरा, अनिश्चितता आ जान अछि जे एखनो बचाओल जा सकैत अछि."

title: Nepal Flood Death Toll Rises as Aid Needs Soar - International Organization for Migration
description: Nepal Flood Death Toll Rises as Aid Needs Soar  International Organization for Migration
publisher.title: International Organization for Migration
full_article:
Kathmandu/Geneva 8 September 2026 – Humanitarian needs are growing rapidly in Nepal after devastating floods last month affected 84,000 people. The death toll has risen to 1,356 while nearly 4,900 remain missing, according to figures reported on 07 September by the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA). Roads, bridges, health facilities, and schools have suffered extensive damage.

As thousands of families struggle with displacement, loss and uncertainty, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) is appealing for USD 20.5 million to assist 43,000 people in support of the Government of Nepal-led response. Aligned with the inter-agency flash appeal launched by the UN and humanitarian partners, IOM's response focuses on strengthening displacement tracking and site coordination, while scaling up shelter, health, and protection assistance for displaced and affected communities.

“For thousands of families, the immediate shock of the floods has been followed by immense uncertainty about their next steps," said Helene Fors, IOM Chief of Mission in Nepal. "Our priority is to ensure that humanitarian action is guided by reliable information and that critical assistance reaches those who need it most.”

IOM teams are already on the ground supporting the response, including in hard-to-reach locations. IOM has conducted initial assessments at holding centres where displaced families are currently residing and has provided critical medicines to health authorities. However, sustained funding is required to expand assistance to affected communities.

Priorities include emergency shelter support, particularly as winter approaches; access to health and psychosocial support services; and targeted protection support for people facing heightened risks, including women, children, older persons, and persons with disabilities.

By expanding the use of its Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM), IOM is also helping authorities to track displacement locations and population movements to identify urgent needs so assistance can be directed where it is needed most. As thousands of displaced people shelter in schools, monasteries, public buildings and host communities, IOM will help ensure they can access assistance, services and protection as co-chair of the Camp Coordination and Camp Management (CCCM) Cluster, led by the Department of Urban Development and Building Construction (DUDBC).

IOM urges the international community to act now and help ensure that affected communities receive the assistance and protection they need.

काठमांडू/जिनेवा ८ सितम्बर २०२६ – नेपालमे पिछला मास विनाशकारी बाढिसँ ८४ हजार लोक प्रभावित भेलाक बाद मानवीय आवश्यकता तेजीसँ बढि रहल अछि । राष्ट्रीय आपदा जोखिम कम करय आ प्रबंधन प्राधिकरण (एनडीआरआरएमए) द्वारा 07 सितंबर कए रिपोर्ट कएल गेल आंकड़ा क अनुसार मृतक क संख्या 1,356 भ गेल अछि जखन कि लगभग 4,900 लापता अछि। सड़क, पुल, स्वास्थ्य सुविधा, आ स्कूल के व्यापक नुकसान भेल अछि.

हजारों परिवार विस्थापन, हानि आ अनिश्चितता स जूझि रहल अछि, नेपाल सरकार के नेतृत्व वाला प्रतिक्रिया के समर्थन में 43 हजार लोक के सहायता के लेल अंतर्राष्ट्रीय प्रवास संगठन (आईओएम) 2 करोड़ 50 लाख डॉलर के अपील क रहल अछि। संयुक्त राष्ट्र आ मानवीय भागीदारक कें द्वारा शुरू कैल गेल अंतर-एजेंसी फ्लैश अपील कें साथ संरेखित, आईओएम कें प्रतिक्रिया विस्थापन ट्रैकिंग आ स्थल समन्वय कें मजबूत करय पर केंद्रित छै, जखन कि विस्थापित आ प्रभावित समुदायक कें लेल आश्रय, स्वास्थ्य, आ सुरक्षा सहायता कें स्केल अप करय छै.

नेपालके आईओएम मिशन प्रमुख हेलेन फोर्स कहलनि जे, हजारों परिवार के लेल बाढ़िक तत्काल झटका के बाद हुनकर अगिला डेग के बारे में अपार अनिश्चितता आयल अछि। "हमरऽ प्राथमिकता ई सुनिश्चित करना छै कि मानवीय कार्रवाई विश्वसनीय जानकारी स॑ निर्देशित होय आरू महत्वपूर्ण सहायता वू लोगऽ तलक पहुँचै जेकरा एकरऽ सबसें जादा जरूरत छै।”

आईओएम केरऽ टीम पहल॑ स॑ ही जमीन प॑ मौजूद छै आरू ई प्रतिक्रिया के समर्थन करी रहलऽ छै, जेकरा म॑ मुश्किल स॑ पहुँचै वाला जगह भी शामिल छै । आईओएम न॑ होल्डिंग सेंटरऽ प॑ प्रारंभिक आकलन करलकै, जहां विस्थापित परिवार अखनी रह॑ छै आरू स्वास्थ्य प्राधिकारी सिनी क॑ महत्वपूर्ण दवाई उपलब्ध कराय देल॑ छै । मुदा प्रभावित समुदायक कें सहायता कें विस्तार कें लेल निरंतर वित्तपोषण कें आवश्यकता छै.

प्राथमिकता मे आपातकालीन आश्रय कें समर्थन शामिल छै, खासकर जखन जाड़ा कें नजदीक आबि रहल छै; स्वास्थ्य आ मनोसामाजिक सहायता सेवाक कें पहुंच; आ महिलाक, बच्चाक, वृद्ध व्यक्तियक आ दिव्यांग व्यक्तियक सहित बढ़ल जोखिम कें सामना करएय वाला लोगक कें लेल लक्षित सुरक्षा समर्थन.

अपन विस्थापन ट्रैकिंग मैट्रिक्स (डीटीएम) कें उपयोग कें विस्तार करयत आईओएम अधिकारियक कें विस्थापन स्थानक आ जनसंख्या कें आवाजाही कें ट्रैक करय मे सेहो मदद कयर रहल छै ताकि तत्काल जरूरतक कें पहचान कैल जा सकय ताकि सहायता कें ओतय निर्देशित कैल जा सकय जतय ओकर बेसि जरूरत छै. जेना-जेना हजारक विस्थापित लोग स्कूलक, मठक, सार्वजनिक भवनक आ मेजबान समुदायक मे आश्रय लैत छै, आईओएम इ सुनिश्चित करय मे मदद करतय की ओ शहरी विकास आ भवन निर्माण विभाग (डीयूडीबीसी) कें नेतृत्व मे शिविर समन्वय आ शिविर प्रबंधन (सीसीसीएम) समूह कें सह-अध्यक्ष कें रूप मे सहायता, सेवाक आ सुरक्षा कें उपयोग कयर सकय छै.

आईओएम अंतरराष्ट्रीय समुदाय सं आग्रह करय छै कि ओ अखन काज करय आ इ सुनिश्चित करय मे मदद करय कि प्रभावित समुदायक कें जरूरत कें सहायता आ सुरक्षा भेटय.

title: A survivor pulled from Nepal’s flood debris after 10 days told rescuers he believes others are still alive, FOX 9 reports — a claim that pushes the operation back from recovery to rescue - Space Daily
description: A survivor pulled from Nepal’s flood debris after 10 days told rescuers he believes others are still alive, FOX 9 reports — a claim that pushes the operation back from recovery to rescue  Space Daily
publisher.title: Space Daily
full_article:
A worker pulled alive from a flooded hydropower tunnel on the Nepal–Tibet border roughly 10 days after the late-August flash floods told rescuers he believed others were still alive inside, FOX 9 Minneapolis-St. Paul reports — a statement that, taken at face value by search teams, pushes the operation’s working assumption back from recovery toward rescue. The distinction is not rhetorical. It governs how fast crews cut, how much risk they accept in unstable ground, and how long a site stays staffed around the clock before it is handed to slower, more methodical debris work.

The floods, which struck the Himalayan border region on or about August 26, 2026, tore through valleys on both sides of the frontier and left hydropower infrastructure — access tunnels, headrace works, construction adits — among the hardest sites to reach and the hardest to give up on. Around day nine to ten, search teams reached two workers alive inside the Trishuli 3A hydropower tunnel. International coverage has named them as Sanjaya (also rendered Sanjay) Shah and Kabir Maharjan; both were airlifted for treatment. Al Jazeera reported that an army spokesperson said one of the men had told rescuers more people remained alive inside. The Guardian reported the same rescue from the tunnel.

That relayed belief — survivor to rescuers to spokesperson to wire — is the reason the story is being carried forward rather than closed out. It is not, at this writing, a confirmation of additional living people underground.

What a late find does to the clock

Every large debris and tunnel search runs on an implicit timetable that nobody posts on a wall. Command staff weigh void space, water, temperature, and the interval since the event, and at some point the balance of probability tips: the mission stops being about people who can be saved and becomes about people who can be found. Resources follow that tip. Medical staging thins, heavy equipment moves in, shift rotations lengthen, and the tempo drops from urgent to deliberate.

A survivor recovered at day 10 does not erase that arithmetic, but it does force a recalculation at the sites where the recovery was made. If one void held people alive through a week and a half, the assumptions used to write off comparable voids nearby become harder to defend. Search leadership is left with a narrower but real question: were the conditions in that tunnel section particular to it, or are they plausible elsewhere in the same complex?

FOX 9’s report on the rescue and what the survivor told his rescuers is here:

The station’s account, drawing on the same regional reporting, frames the rescue against the scale authorities have described: more than 5,000 people reported missing, including dozens of Americans, and hundreds of workers believed trapped in tunnels along the affected corridor. Those figures come from agencies working an active, unstable disaster zone, and they have moved from day to day. They should be read as reported totals under revision, not as settled accounting.

A belief relayed is not a rescue confirmed

The care required here is specific. What exists is a survivor’s statement, made after roughly 10 days in a flooded tunnel, relayed by rescuers and then by an army spokesperson to reporters. What does not exist — and what nothing in the current record supports — is confirmation that additional people are alive at that site.

The gap between those two things matters to families reading coverage in Kathmandu, in the border districts, and abroad. A man in that situation may have heard voices, may have been separated from colleagues before losing contact, may be reporting what he knew to be true when he last had information, hours or days before he was reached. Any of those is consistent with the account as relayed. None of them, on its own, establishes that others survived to the point of rescue.

Officials have been careful in similar terms. Communications Minister Bikram Timilsina, per wire coverage, expressed hope that more people would be brought out alive — a statement of intent and possibility, not a claim of contact with anyone still underground. Hope, in a disaster-command context, is a legitimate input into resource decisions. It is not evidence, and it has not been offered as evidence.

What “rescue, not recovery” means on the ground

Operationally, the posture shift is less about new tactics than about time and priority. A rescue posture keeps a site at the front of the queue for personnel and equipment, keeps medical evacuation capacity on standby, and holds open the tolerance for working in conditions that a recovery operation would slow down to avoid. It shortens the interval between deciding to open a section and actually opening it.

It also changes how negative findings are treated. Under recovery logic, an empty void closes a question. Under rescue logic, it moves the search to the next void without lowering the assumed urgency. That difference compounds over days, and in a corridor where hundreds of workers are reported unaccounted for across multiple tunnel sites, it determines the order in which those sites are reached.

Nothing in the current record guarantees that order will produce another live rescue. The floods were severe, the terrain is difficult, and the reported missing counts remain large enough that most of the search will not end in the way this one section did. What the survivor’s account has done, as FOX 9 and the wires have reported it, is deny search leadership the option of assuming otherwise — of treating the tunnels as closed on the strength of elapsed time alone. For now, the assumption on the ground is that someone may still be waiting, and the operation is being run accordingly.

अगस्त के अंत में आयल आकस्मिक बाढ़ के लगभग 10 दिन बाद नेपाल–तिब्बत सीमा पर बाढ़ि स भरल जलविद्युत सुरंग स जिंदा खींच लेल गेल एकटा मजदूर बचावकर्ता सब के कहलक जे ओकर मानब अछि जे अंदर एखनो दोसर लोक जीवित अछि, फॉक्स 9 मिनियापोलिस-सेंट. पॉल रिपोर्ट करै छै — एक बयान जे खोज टीम द्वारा फेस वैल्यू पर लेलऽ जाय छै, ऑपरेशन केरऽ कामकाजी धारणा क॑ रिकवरी स॑ वापस बचाव के तरफ धकेल॑ छै । भेद अलंकारिक नहि अछि। ई नियंत्रित करै छै कि चालक दल कतेक तेजी स॑ कटौती करै छै, अस्थिर जमीन म॑ कतेक जोखिम क॑ स्वीकार करै छै, आरू कोनो साइट क॑ धीमा, अधिक विधिवत मलबा के काम म॑ सौंपला स॑ पहल॑ चौबीसों घंटा कर्मचारी स॑ भरलऽ रहै छै ।

हिमालयी सीमा क्षेत्र म॑ २६ अगस्त २०२६ या ओकरऽ आसपास आबी गेलऽ ई बाढ़ न॑ सीमा केरऽ दोनों तरफ के घाटी क॑ फाड़ी क॑ जलविद्युत बुनियादी ढाँचा — पहुँच सुरंग, हेडरेस के काम, निर्माण एडिट — पहुँचना सबस॑ कठिन आरू हार मानना ​​सबस॑ कठिन जगहऽ म॑ शामिल करी देलकै । नौ स दस दिन क आसपास तलाशी टीम त्रिशुली 3ए जलविद्युत सुरंग क अंदर जिंदा दूटा मजदूर तक पहुंच गेल। अंतर्राष्ट्रीय कवरेज में हुनका सब के नाम संजय (संजय सेहो कहल गेल अछि) शाह आ कबीर महर्जन के रूप में राखल गेल अछि; दुनू गोटे के इलाज के लेल एयरलिफ्ट क देल गेल। अल जजीरा के खबर छै कि सेना के प्रवक्ता के कहना छै कि एक आदमी न॑ बचावकर्ता सिनी क॑ बतैलकै कि भीतर स॑ आरू लोग जिंदा छै । गार्जियन सुरंग स इएह बचाव क सूचना देलक।

ओ रिले विश्वास — बचावकर्ता सं बचि गेल सं ल क प्रवक्ता सं तार धरि — एकर कारण अछि जे कहानी के बंद करय सं बेसी आगू बढ़ाओल जा रहल अछि. ई, ई लेखन के समय, भूमिगत अतिरिक्त जीवित लोगऽ के पुष्टि नै छै ।

लेट खोज घड़ी के केहन करैत अछि

हर पैघ मलबा आ सुरंगक खोज एकटा अन्तर्निहित समय सारिणी पर चलैत अछि जे कियो कोनो देबाल पर पोस्ट नहि करैत अछि । कमांड स्टाफ शून्य स्थान, पानी, तापमान, आरू घटना के बाद के अंतराल के तौल करै छै, आरू कोनो समय संभावना के संतुलन के टिप्स: मिशन ऐन्हऽ लोगऽ के बारे म॑ होना बंद करी दै छै जेकरा बचालऽ जाब॑ सकै छै आरू वू लोगऽ के बारे म॑ बनी जाय छै जेकरा मिल॑ सकै छै । संसाधन ओहि टिप के पालन करैत अछि। मेडिकल स्टेजिंग पतला भ जाइत अछि, भारी उपकरण अंदर आबि जाइत अछि, शिफ्ट रोटेशन लंबा भ जाइत अछि, आ टेम्पो जरूरी सं सोचल-समझल भ जाइत अछि.

10म दिन बरामद भेल व्यक्ति ओ अंकगणित नहि मेटाबैत अछि, मुदा ओहि ठाम पुनर्गणना करबा लेल मजबूर करैत अछि जतय बरामदगी भेल छल। जँ एकटा शून्यता डेढ़ सप्ताह धरि लोक केँ जीवित राखि दैत छल त' लग मे तुलनीय शून्यता केँ लिखबा लेल प्रयोग कयल जायवला धारणा सभक बचाव करब कठिन भ' जाइत अछि. खोज नेतृत्व एकटा संकीर्ण मुदा वास्तविक प्रश्नक संग रहि जाइत अछि : की ओहि सुरंग खंडक परिस्थिति ओकरा लेल विशेष छल , वा ओही परिसर मे आन ठाम प्लाजिबल अछि ?

बचाव के बारे में FOX 9 केरऽ रिपोर्ट आरू बची गेलऽ आदमी न॑ अपनऽ बचावकर्ता सिनी क॑ की कहलकै, यहाँ छै:

स्टेशन केरऽ खाता, वू ही क्षेत्रीय रिपोर्टिंग क॑ आकर्षित करी क॑, अधिकारियऽ न॑ वर्णित पैमाना के खिलाफ बचाव केरऽ फ्रेम बनाबै छै: ५,००० स॑ भी अधिक लोगऽ क॑ लापता होय के रिपोर्ट देलऽ गेलऽ छै, जेकरा म॑ दर्जनों अमेरिकी भी शामिल छै, आरू सैकड़ों मजदूर प्रभावित गलियारा के किनारे सुरंगऽ म॑ फंसलऽ मानलऽ जाय रहलऽ छै । ओ आंकड़ा सक्रिय, अस्थिर आपदा क्षेत्र मे काज करय वाला एजेंसी सं आयल अछि, आओर ओ दिन-प्रतिदिन बढ़ैत रहल अछि. ओकरा संशोधन कें तहत रिपोर्ट कैल गेल कुल कें रूप मे पढ़ल जेबाक चाही, निपटारा लेखा कें रूप मे नहि.

रिले कएल गेल मान्यता कोनो बचावक पुष्टि नहि अछि

एतय जे देखभाल कें आवश्यकता छै, ओ विशिष्ट छै. जे मौजूद छै, वू छै एगो बची गेलऽ लोगऽ के बयान, जे बाढ़ स॑ भरलऽ सुरंग म॑ लगभग 10 दिन के बाद देलऽ गेलऽ छै, जेकरा बचावकर्ता आरू ओकरा बाद सेना केरऽ प्रवक्ता न॑ पत्रकारऽ क॑ रिले करलकै । जे मौजूद नै छै — आरू जेकरऽ समर्थन वर्तमान रिकॉर्ड म॑ कुछ भी नै करै छै — वू ई बात के पुष्टि छै कि वू जगह प॑ अतिरिक्त लोग जीवित छै ।

काठमांडू, सीमावर्ती जिला, आ विदेश मे कवरेज पढ़य वाला परिवार के लेल ओहि दुनू चीज के बीच के अंतर मायने रखैत अछि. ओहि स्थिति मे कोनो आदमी आवाज सुनने होयत, संपर्क गमाबय सं पहिने सहयोगी सं अलग भ गेल होयत, ओ रिपोर्ट क रहल होयत जे ओकरा अंतिम बेर जानकारी भेटला पर, ओकरा सं पहुंचय सं घंटों या दिन पहिने, सही बुझल छल. ओहि मे सं कोनो खाता के अनुरूप अछि जेना कि रिले कएल गेल अछि. कोनो भी, अपनऽ दम पर, ई स्थापित नै करै छै कि दोसरऽ लोग बचाव के हद तक बचलै ।

अधिकारी सब सेहो एहने शब्द मे सावधान रहल छथि। संचार मंत्री बिक्रम तिमिल्सिना, प्रति तार कवरेज, आशा व्यक्त करलकै कि आरू लोगऽ क॑ जिंदा बाहर लानलऽ जैतै — इरादा आरू संभावना केरऽ बयान, नै कि अभी भी भूमिगत ककरो स॑ संपर्क के दावा । आशा, आपदा-कमांड संदर्भ मे, संसाधन निर्णय मे एकटा वैध इनपुट छै. ई प्रमाण नै छै, आ नै प्रमाण के रूप में पेश करलऽ गेलऽ छै ।

जमीन पर “बचाव, रिकवरी नहि” के की मतलब होइत छैक

परिचालनात्मक रूप स॑ मुद्रा परिवर्तन समय आरू प्राथमिकता के तुलना म॑ नया रणनीति के बारे म॑ कम छै । बचाव मुद्रा कर्मी आ उपकरणक कें लेल कतार कें सामने एकटा साइट कें रखयत छै, मेडिकल निकासी क्षमता कें स्टैंडबाई पर रखयत छै, आ ऐहन परिस्थितिक मे काम करय कें लेल सहिष्णुता कें खुलल रखयत छै, जेकरा सं बचय कें लेल रिकवरी ऑपरेशन धीमा भ जायत. ई कोनों खंड खोलै के फैसला आरू वास्तव म॑ ओकरा खोलै के बीच के अंतराल क॑ कम करी दै छै ।

एकरा स॑ ई भी बदलाव आबै छै कि नकारात्मक निष्कर्षऽ के साथ कोन तरह के व्यवहार करलऽ जाय छै । रिकवरी लॉजिक के तहत एकटा खाली शून्यता कोनो सवाल के बंद क दैत अछि. बचाव तर्क के तहत ई अनुमानित तात्कालिकता के कम केने बिना खोज के अगिला शून्य में ल जाय छै. ओ अंतर दिनक संग आओर बढ़ि जाइत अछि, आ एकटा एहन गलियारा मे जतय सैकड़ों मजदूर कए कईटा सुरंग स्थल पर बेहिसाब रिपोर्ट भेटैत अछि, इ निर्धारित करैत अछि जे ओहि स्थल पर कोन क्रम मे पहुंचल जाइत अछि ।

वर्तमान रिकॉर्ड मे कोनो बात इ गारंटी नहि दैत अछि जे एहि आदेश स एकटा आओर लाइव बचाव पैदा होएत। बाढ़ि भयंकर छल, इलाका कठिन अछि, आ रिपोर्ट कयल गेल लापता गिनती एतेक पैघ अछि जे अधिकांश खोज ओहिना नहिं समाप्त होयत जेना एहि एकटा खंड में भेल छल. बचे वाला के खाता जे करलकै, जेना कि फॉक्स 9 आरू तारऽ न॑ एकरऽ रिपोर्ट करलकै, वू छै खोज नेतृत्व क॑ ई विकल्प स॑ वंचित करै छै कि वू अन्यथा मान॑ — असगरे बीतलऽ समय के बल प॑ सुरंगऽ क॑ बंद मान॑ । फिलहाल जमीन पर इ धारणा अछि जे एखनो कियो इंतजार क रहल भ सकैत अछि, आ तदनुसार ऑपरेशन भ रहल अछि।

description: Nepal marks 1 year since Gen Z-led violent revolt against corruption  africanews.com
publisher.title: africanews.com
full_article:
Tuesday marked a year since Gen Z-led violent protests against widespread corruption in Nepal forced the then prime minister, K.P. Sharma Oli to resign.

Several people showed up at an event in Kathmandu to honor the memories of those who lost their lives in the protest by offering fruits and flowers.

The upheaval began last September, when youth-led protests over corruption and a social media ban spiraled into violence. Security forces opened fire on demonstrators, killing dozens, while government buildings and politicians’ homes were set ablaze.

Pratish Shrestha, an injured protester called for help from the Nepal government and said "we still need support, we still have injuries and are bound to wheelchairs and clutches. That is why we need the state to take care of us until the end of our lives.”

Then on August 26, catastrophic floods hit the country, killing more than 1,300 people, with nearly 5,000 missing and causing an estimated $2.56 billion in damage.

For a country with a $50 billion economy, the loss is enormous.

The new government must now rebuild damaged infrastructure and get the country back on track after months of instability.

full_article:
Join Dave Weixelman for an evening of highlights and stories of his 10-day trek to the Langtang Valley in Nepal in fall 2025. The trip provided an incredible, immersive experience in one of the most beautiful places on earth. Highlights of his trip included visiting the city of Bhaktapur, near Kathmandu, visiting temples and palaces in Durbar Square, and trekking to villages in the high Himalayan mountains. Dave enjoyed botanizing and seeing the diverse flora in the mountains of Nepal.

Be the first to know, sign up for our newsletter, absolutely free of course. Sign Up

He will also update us about the disastrous flood, which occurred recently on August 26. It was triggered by a massive glacier-related collapse that caused catastrophic flash flooding across multiple districts, including the area of his 2025 trek, near the village of Syabrubesi on the Bhote Koshi River area of Nepal, one of the hardest hit areas in the flooding.

Donations to CATS received that evening will be donated to the Nepal/Tibet relief efforts.

The public is welcome to meet the presenter and enjoy cookies afterwards. Dave obtained a B.A. degree in Botany and an M.S. degree in Natural Resources Management from the University of Alaska, Fairbanks. Now retired, he was a botanist with the U.S. Forest Service for 37 years. Dave’s hobbies include botany, astronomy and hiking, especially in the high mountains of North America and, most recently, in Nepal.

title: Nepal says big polluters must ‘wake up’ as it calls for climate compensation over flood disaster - The Guardian
description: Nepal says big polluters must ‘wake up’ as it calls for climate compensation over flood disaster  The Guardian
publisher.title: The Guardian
full_article:
Nepal is demanding $20m in climate compensation for the recent devastating floods, as a senior minister called on the world’s most polluting countries to “wake up” and accept shared responsibility for a disaster that led to the death or disappearance of more than 6,000 people.

Scientists believe the climate crisis had a role to play in the floods, which were triggered when a melting glacier partially collapsed and set off a deadly landslide and flash flooding through Chinese-controlled Tibet and Nepal in late August. So far, more than 1,300 are confirmed dead and more than 5,500 still missing, with hopes of their survival diminished after 12 days of rescue operations.

A journey to the frontline of Nepal’s disastrous floods – podcast Read more

Speaking to the Guardian, Nepal’s foreign minister, Shisir Khanal, was forthright in his call for climate justice and said it was imperative the world’s biggest economies stepped up to help Nepal recover and rebuild after the catastrophic floods.

Nepal contributes less than 0.1% of global greenhouse gas emissions, while its neighbours India and China are among the world’s biggest emitters. The mountains of the Himalayas – which span across India, China, Nepal and Bhutan – have been warming at a rate nearly 50% faster than the global average.

In 2023, the UN said Nepal’s mountains had lost close to a third of their ice in just over 30 years due to global heating.

Khanal emphasised that the recent disaster was far more extreme than any flooding regularly seen during the monsoon season, and said the magnitude of damage was on par with the 2015 earthquake that left much of the country in ruins.

View image in fullscreen An excavator repairs a damaged road in Nepal near the Trishuli River on Monday. Photograph: Anushree Fadnavis/Reuters

“This felt like a tsunami that was coming from the Himalayas,” he said. “We experienced waves as high as 60, 70 feet, which were mixed with debris, mud, stones, rocks, and came at the speed of almost 180km per hour. Towns, villages and highways were completely wiped out and there are some areas still disconnected.”

Khanal confirmed that Nepal’s ministry of finance and ministry of environment had written a joint letter to the UN’s fund for responding to loss and damage – which was set up in 2022 in line with the Paris climate agreement – to request $20m in climate-related damages.

“We have contributed so little to climate change,” he said. “It is imperative for those in the global community who benefit from larger, much more polluting economies, and whose historical contribution to greenhouse gases is much bigger than ours, to accept a shared responsibility. This affects all of humanity.”

For Nepal, the disaster was particularly worrying because it was “one of the strongest warning signals that we’ve experienced of what’s to come”, he said.

“The global community should not see this as one-off disaster; it should be viewed in the context of the changing climate in the Himalayas,” he said. “We know it is going to be a recurring scenario that more and more communities, not just in Nepal but around the world, will have to face.”

Khanal acknowledged that the compensation amount Nepal has requested from the UN was “obviously not nearly enough to cover the damage that we have sustained”. According to some estimates, the total damage caused by the floods will be upwards of $5bn, though Khanal said it could be even higher.

Upwards of 20,000 homes will probably have to be rebuilt, as well as the main highway. Villages built in vulnerable areas along the river, some of which washed away entirely, may have to be relocated to higher, safer ground.

While Khanal initially singled out India and China as countries that should step in to help – while avoiding mention of the US, which is the world’s biggest polluter – he rowed back on those comments, saying: “It is not just about shifting the blame to one or the other country, it’s about us all working together.”

View image in fullscreen Damaged buildings on the banks of the Trishuli River. Photograph: Anushree Fadnavis/Reuters

He emphasised that the compensation demand was also meant to act as a “wake-up call for the global community to establish a more robust mechanism to help vulnerable and small economies like Nepal”.

After the flood: human suffering on an unfathomable scale in Nepal’s worst-hit districts Read more

The UN has admitted the loss and damage fund is already facing a “significant financing gap”. The fund has already received requests totalling $2.8bn from about 119 countries, but so far only around $400m has been given by the international community. The US has given just $17m, after Donald Trump withdrew from the Paris agreement.

Khanal acknowledged there were “political challenges” in getting Nepal the climate compensation it was demanding.

“Yes there always will be people who may not agree to our perspective or deny there is climate change, but there are also people who deny that the Earth is round,” he said bluntly.

He emphasised the importance of funds being made available not just for immediate disaster response but also for preparedness and mitigation for climate-related risk.

Khanal rebuffed allegations that China had failed to give an adequate warning or share data with Nepal about the impending floods. He said he was in discussion with China about enhancing coordination and data sharing for the Himalayan region.

“With the benefit of hindsight, we can now see that this glacier was fragile and had been receding in the past six months,” he said.

“But before the floods hit, there was no knowledge on our part, or on the part of Chinese scientists, that this particular collapse was imminent. I do not believe any of us had any idea of the threat until it happened.”

नेपाल हाल केरऽ विनाशकारी बाढ़ केरऽ जलवायु मुआवजा के २० मिलियन डॉलर के मांग करी रहलऽ छै, कैन्हेंकि एगो वरिष्ठ मंत्री न॑ दुनिया केरऽ सबसें प्रदूषक देशऽ स॑ “जाग” आरू ऐसनऽ आपदा केरऽ साझा जिम्मेदारी स्वीकार करै के आह्वान करलकै जेकरा म॑ ६,००० स॑ भी अधिक लोगऽ के मौत या गायब होय गेलऽ छेलै ।

वैज्ञानिकऽ के मानना ​​छै कि ई बाढ़ म॑ जलवायु संकट के भूमिका छेलै, जेकरऽ शुरुआत अगस्त के अंत म॑ चीन द्वारा नियंत्रित तिब्बत आरू नेपाल के माध्यम स॑ घातक भूस्खलन आरू झटका लगै वाला ग्लेशियर के आंशिक रूप स॑ गिरला स॑ शुरू होलै । एखन धरि 1300 सं बेसी के मौत के पुष्टि भ गेल अछि आओर 5500 सं बेसी लोक एखनो लापता अछि, 12 दिन के बचाव अभियान के बाद हुनकर जीवित रहय के उम्मीद कम भ गेल अछि.

नेपाल के विनाशकारी बाढ़ के मोर्चा पर एक यात्रा – podcast Read more

गार्जियन स॑ बात करतें हुअ॑ नेपाल केरऽ विदेश मंत्री शिसिर खनाल न॑ जलवायु न्याय केरऽ आह्वान म॑ सीधा-सीधा कहलकै आरू कहलकै कि विनाशकारी बाढ़ के बाद नेपाल क॑ ठीक करै आरू पुनर्निर्माण म॑ मदद करै लेली दुनिया केरऽ सबसें बड़ऽ अर्थव्यवस्था न॑ कदम बढ़ाबै के जरूरत छै ।

वैश्विक ग्रीनहाउस गैस उत्सर्जन मे नेपाल के योगदान 0.1% सं कम अछि, जखन कि ओकर पड़ोसी देश भारत आ चीन दुनिया के सबस पैघ उत्सर्जन करय वाला देश मे शामिल अछि. हिमालय केरऽ पहाड़ – जे पूरा भारत, चीन, नेपाल आरू भूटान म॑ फैललऽ छै – वैश्विक औसत स॑ लगभग ५०% तेजी स॑ गरम होय रहलऽ छै ।

2023 मे संयुक्त राष्ट्र कहलक जे ग्लोबल हीटिंग के कारण नेपाल के पहाड़ मे 30 साल सं किछ बेसि समय मे करीब एक तिहाई बर्फ के नुकसान भ गेल अछि.

खनाल न॑ ई बात प॑ जोर देलकै कि हाल केरऽ आपदा मानसून के मौसम म॑ नियमित रूप स॑ देखलऽ जाय वाला कोनो भी बाढ़ स॑ कहीं अधिक चरम छै, आरू कहलकै कि नुकसान केरऽ परिमाण २०१५ केरऽ भूकंप के बराबर छै जेकरा स॑ देश केरऽ बहुत हिस्सा खंडहर होय गेलऽ छेलै ।

View image in fullscreen सोमदिन नेपालमे त्रिशूली नदीक समीप क्षतिग्रस्त सड़कक मरम्मत करैत एक एक्सकेवेटर। फोटोग्राफ : अनुश्री फडणवीस/रायटर

ओ कहलनि जे, ई सुनामी जेकाँ लागल जे हिमालय स आबि रहल छल। “हमरा सब के 60, 70 फीट तक के लहर के अनुभव भेल, जे मलबा, थाल, पाथर, चट्टान स मिश्रित छल, आ लगभग 180 किमी प्रति घंटा के रफ्तार स आयल छल। शहर, गाम आ राजमार्ग पूरा तरह स सफाया भ गेल छल आ किछु इलाका एखनो टूटल अछि।”

खनाल न॑ ई बात के पुष्टि करलकै कि नेपाल केरऽ वित्त मंत्रालय आरू पर्यावरण मंत्रालय न॑ नुकसान आरू क्षति केरऽ जवाब दै लेली संयुक्त राष्ट्र केरऽ कोष क॑ संयुक्त पत्र लिखलकै – जे पेरिस जलवायु समझौता के अनुरूप २०२२ म॑ स्थापित करलऽ गेलऽ छेलै – जलवायु संबंधी क्षति केरऽ २० मिलियन डॉलर के आग्रह करै लेली ।

ओ कहला जे जलवायु परिवर्तन मे हमर सबहक योगदान एतेक कम अछि। "वैश्विक समुदाय म॑ जे लोगऽ क॑ बड़ऽ, बहुत अधिक प्रदूषणकारी अर्थव्यवस्था स॑ फायदा मिलै छै, आरू जेकरऽ ग्रीनहाउस गैसऽ म॑ ऐतिहासिक योगदान हमरऽ स॑ बहुत बड़ऽ छै, ओकरा लेली ई जरूरी छै कि वू साझा जिम्मेदारी क॑ स्वीकार करै ।ई सब मानवता क॑ प्रभावित करै छै ।"

ओ कहलनि जे, नेपाल के लेल ई आपदा विशेष रूप सं चिंताजनक छल, किया कि ई “आबय वाला बात के सबस मजबूत चेतावनी संकेत मे सं एक छल जे हमरा सब के अनुभव भेल अछि”.

ओ कहलनि जे, वैश्विक समुदाय के एकरा एक बेर के आपदा के रूप में नै देखबाक चाही, एकरा हिमालय के बदलैत जलवायु के संदर्भ में देखबाक चाही। “हमरा सब के पता छै कि ई एगो आवर्ती परिदृश्य होबै वाला छै जेकरऽ सामना खाली नेपाल म॑ ही नै बल्कि दुनिया भर म॑ अधिक स॑ अधिक समुदाय क॑ करना पड़ी जैतै ।”

खनाल न॑ स्वीकार करलकै कि नेपाल न॑ संयुक्त राष्ट्र स॑ जे मुआवजा के राशि मँगल॑ छै, वू “जाहिर छै कि हमरा सिनी क॑ जे नुकसान पहुँचैलऽ गेलऽ छै ओकरा पूरा करै लेली लगभग पर्याप्त नै छेलै” । किछु अनुमान क अनुसार बाढ़ि स कुल नुकसान 5 अरब डॉलर स ऊपर होएत, हालांकि खनाल कहला जे इ आओर बेसी भ सकैत अछि।

संभवतः 20 हजार स ऊपर घर कए फेर स बनाबय पड़त, संगहि मुख्य राजमार्ग सेहो। नदी कें किनारे कमजोर क्षेत्रक मे बनल गामक कें, जेकरा मे सं किच्छू पूरा तरह सं बह गेलय, ओकरा ऊँच, सुरक्षित जमीन पर स्थानांतरित करय पड़य सकय छै.

खनाल न॑ शुरू म॑ भारत आरू चीन क॑ ऐन्हऽ देश के रूप म॑ एकल करलकै जेकरा मदद करै लेली कदम रखै के चाही – जबकि दुनिया केरऽ सबस॑ बड़ऽ प्रदूषक देश अमेरिका केरऽ जिक्र स॑ बचै के साथ-साथ हुनी वू टिप्पणी प॑ वापसी करतें हुअ॑ कहलकै कि “ई खाली दोष एक या दोसरऽ देश प॑ डालै के बात नै छै, ई हम्मं॑ सब मिल क॑ काम करै के बात छै ।”

फुलस्क्रीन में छवि देखें त्रिशूली नदी के किनारे क्षतिग्रस्त भवन | फोटोग्राफ : अनुश्री फडणवीस/रायटर

हुनी ई बात प॑ जोर देलकै कि मुआवजा के मांग के उद्देश्य भी “वैश्विक समुदाय लेली एगो जागरण के आह्वान छै कि वू नेपाल जैसनऽ कमजोर आरू छोटऽ अर्थव्यवस्था के मदद लेली एगो अधिक मजबूत तंत्र स्थापित करै” ।

बाढ़िक बाद : नेपालक सबसँ बेसी प्रभावित जिला मे अथाह पैमाना पर मानवीय दुख Read more

संयुक्त राष्ट्र न॑ स्वीकार करलकै कि नुकसान आरू नुकसान केरऽ कोष म॑ पहल॑ स॑ ही “महत्वपूर्ण वित्तपोषण अंतर” के सामना करना पड़॑ छै । एहि कोष कए करीब 119 देश स कुल 2.8 अरब डॉलर क अनुरोध भेट चुकल अछि, मुदा एखन धरि अंतरराष्ट्रीय समुदाय स मात्र करीब 400 करोड़ डॉलर देल गेल अछि। पेरिस समझौता स॑ डोनाल्ड ट्रंप केरऽ हटला के बाद अमेरिका न॑ महज १७ मिलियन डॉलर देल॑ छै ।

खनाल स्वीकार केलथि जे नेपाल कए जे जलवायु मुआवजा मांगल जा रहल अछि ओकरा भेटबा मे “राजनीतिक चुनौती” अछि।

हुनी बेबाक तरीका स॑ कहलकै, “हँ हमेशा ऐन्हऽ लोग रहतै जे शायद हमरऽ नजरिया स॑ सहमत नै होतै या जलवायु परिवर्तन स॑ इनकार करै छै, लेकिन ऐसनऽ लोग भी छै जे ई बात स॑ इनकार करै छै कि पृथ्वी गोल छै ।

हुनी न सिर्फ आपदा के तत्काल प्रतिक्रिया लेली नै बल्कि जलवायु संबंधी जोखिम के तैयारी आरू कम करै लेली भी धन उपलब्ध करै के महत्व प जोर देलकै ।

खनाल नेपाल के साथ आसन्न बाढ़ के बारे में पर्याप्त चेतावनी या आंकड़ा साझा नै करला के आरोप के खारिज करलकै । हुनी कहलकै कि हुनी चीन के साथ हिमालय क्षेत्र लेली समन्वय आरू डाटा शेयरिंग बढ़ाबै के बारे मँ चर्चा करी रहलौ छै ।

ओ कहला जे पाछु कए देखला क फायदा स आब हम देख सकैत छी जे इ ग्लेशियर नाजुक छल आ पिछला छह मास स इ हटि रहल छल।

"मुदा बाढ़ि सँ पहिने हमरा सभक दिस सँ, वा चीनी वैज्ञानिक सभक दिस सँ कोनो जानकारी नहि छल जे ई विशेष पतन आसन्न अछि। हमरा विश्वास नहि अछि जे जा धरि ई नहि भेल ता धरि हमरा सभ मे सँ किनको एहि खतरा केर कोनो अंदाजा नहि छल।"

Mary Sorensen, a 60-year-old environmental consultant who hails from just north of Atlanta, had traveled to Mount Kailash on a spiritual pilgrimage her family called a "bucket list" trip.

"She was with a group called Isha that she does yoga with, and she prays with, and she meditates with," her son, Riley Wildeman, told ABC News.

The Georgia mom and grandmother managed to complete her journey and was reportedly on her way back down the mountain when tragedy struck. She told her son that the long trip home would give her time to reflect on her time spent abroad before returning to Georgia.

"The last thing that she sent to us was Tuesday [Aug.25] morning, and she was on her way down the mountain," Wildeman recalled.

Sorensen's son later noted how his mom wrapped the poignant message in retrospect.

"She ended that text by saying, 'I'm so grateful that you guys are my family,'" he added.

The next day, relentless floods swept through the Nepal-Tibet border region, reportedly triggering deadly landslides across the region. To date, 1,287 have died, and more than 5,000 are still missing due to the disaster, per the BBC.

Regardless, Sorensen's family still held on to hope that she might have survived.

Son Recalls Father Calling With News of His Mom Going Missing in Deadly Floods in Nepal

Wildeman, a public school teacher, told ABC News about the moment his father called with the tragic news.

"There was really very little about where they were, about where the flood had hit, about how severe the flood was," he recalled. "And then all the news coverage and all the videos and all of the social media popped up, and so that's how we kind of understood the severity of the situation."

Children attend a gathering to observe a national day of mourning for victims of flash floods in Kathmandu on September 7, 2026. (Photo by Prakash MATHEMA / AFP via Getty Images)

He and his family went on to exhaust every avenue they could think of to locate Sorensen amid the disaster.

"We've called in every favor and every possible thing that we can call in," he told ABC News.

"We feel so much heartbreak and so much sadness and pain, like a deep, guttural pain," Wilderman added. "My whole family and my mom all believe in a God that does miracles, and that the miracle that we're gonna get out of this is gonna be something that we might not necessarily understand right now, but it's gonna be something that we look back on and we feel."

Yesterday, Nepalis held a day of mourning for those lost in the floods.

अटलांटा केरऽ ठीक उत्तर म॑ रह॑ वाला ६० वर्षीय पर्यावरण सलाहकार मैरी सोरेंसन न॑ एगो आध्यात्मिक तीर्थयात्रा प॑ माउंट कैलाश गेलऽ छेली जेकरा हुनकऽ परिवार न॑ “बकेट लिस्ट” यात्रा कहल॑ छै ।

हुनकऽ बेटा रिले वाइल्डमैन न॑ एबीसी न्यूज क॑ बतैलकै कि हुनी ईशा नाम केरऽ एगो ग्रुप के साथ छेली जेकरा स॑ हुनी योग करै छै, आरू ओकरा साथ प्रार्थना करै छै, आरू ओकरा साथ ध्यान करै छै ।

जॉर्जिया केरऽ मम्मी आरू दादी अपनऽ यात्रा पूरा करै म॑ सफल रहलै आरू खबर छै कि वू वापस पहाड़ स॑ नीचें जाय रहलऽ छेली जब॑ त्रासदी आबी गेलै । ओ अपन बेटा के कहलखिन जे घर के लंबा यात्रा सं हुनका जॉर्जिया वापसी सं पहिने विदेश मे बिताओल समय पर चिंतन करय के समय मिलत.

वाइल्डमैन स्मरण करैत कहलनि जे, अंतिम चीज जे ओ हमरा सब लग पठेने छलीह, ओ मंगल दिन [25 अगस्त] भोर छल, आ ओ पहाड़ स नीचा उतरबाक रास्ता पर छलीह।

बाद में सोरेंसन के बेटा नोट केलक जे कोना ओकर मम्मी पाछू घुमि क' देखला पर मार्मिक संदेश के लपेटि लेलक.

ओ आगू कहलनि जे, ओ ओहि पाठ के समाप्त करैत कहलीह जे हम एतेक आभारी छी जे अहाँ सब हमर परिवार छी।

title: How the Nepal-Tibet disaster became the latest victim of China’s ‘Clean Internet’ campaign - The Guardian
description: How the Nepal-Tibet disaster became the latest victim of China’s ‘Clean Internet’ campaign  The Guardian
publisher.title: The Guardian
full_article:
T sering Phuntsok watched news of the Nepal-Tibet flood unfold from thousands of miles away in southern India. The 46-year-old Tibetan in exile has missing family members on both sides of the border; those in Nepal are named in official government lists, but in Tibet he has received no information.

“I have started praying for the lost ones now. I have to accept they will not return [because] … I’m not getting any information.”

Rescuers in Nepal find two more people alive after flash flood disaster Read more

The flooding disaster is an example of the increasing use by Chinese authorities of “Clean Internet 2026”, the latest version of a long-running campaign by the Ministry of Public Security that criminalises anything officials regard as false information, which includes unofficial accounts of the floods.

It follows a well-established playbook in which authorities promote official narratives, suppress independent accounts, discourage efforts to look back at the causes of a disaster and punish those who post claims that differ from the government-approved narrative.

While earlier versions of the campaign focused on cybercrime and hacking, it is increasingly being used to target what the authorities call “rumours” which include unofficial information about the disaster.

“The campaign serves a dual purpose. Tackling genuine problems like fraud and misinformation while tightening control over public narratives,” says Tencho Gyatso from the International Campaign for Tibet, a US based Tibetan advocacy group. “That dual purpose is what makes it more nuanced and challenging to criticise.”

In the hours after the floods, researchers say they saw a huge surge in interest across Chinese social media. The topic was trending, but then fell away as comments were removed in real time.

View image in fullscreen Flowers are placed on mud as a tribute at the disaster-hit area at Gyirong Port. Photograph: Tingshu Wang/Pool Reuters/AP

Screenshots seen by the Guardian show the Chinese app WeChat restricting posts about the floods. In one case, a user was notified by WeChat that a post about the flooding had been reported and then deleted for containing “politically sensitive content”. Another was stopped from being shared. It was said to be “unavailable due to policy violation” and that it contained “prohibited content”.

“[The trend] was constantly shifting and being manipulated because there was real interest,” says David Bandurski, director of the China Media Project, a research group that monitors Chinese media. “A ‘crackdown’ is not the right word, because they don’t crack down. It’s a consistent, persistent, everyday application of a policy of public-opinion guidance.”

On 30 August, four days after the disaster, police in Tibet reported 10 cases under the Clean Internet 2026 campaign relating to “rumours” about the disaster. In the majority of cases there were claims that more than 1,000 people had been swept away in the floods. So far, Chinese authorities have released a death toll of 43. Human rights and Tibetan advocacy groups have accused the Chinese government of concealing the true scale of the death toll.

The police notice said that spreading of “rumours” “misleads the public and disrupts online order” and it intended to “ensure that disaster relief work proceeds smoothly”.

A user from Jiangxi, a province 3,000km away from the disaster, posted on a video platform claiming “the number of missing people had risen to 826”. According to the police report the user faced “administrative punishment” without specifying what that involved.

‘Proving that the state is working hard’

One former Chinese state media journalist, who agreed to speak on the condition of anonymity for fear of reprisals, says control in times of crisis also works through simple omission of information as much as suppression: “Official news coverage devotes enormous space to proving that the state is working hard, but gives very little information answering the most basic questions: who is missing? Where were they last seen? Which buildings have been searched?

“Controls have become much stricter, especially regarding the internet, though there are nuances, as there are still ways to bypass restrictions. For instance, by posting quickly or using veiled language to get content through,” they say.

But allowing some reporting can serve the interests of central authorities, says one former CGTN editor who worked at the broadcaster during the Covid pandemic and who also asked not to be named for fear of reprisals.

View image in fullscreen Police have punished people for spreading unofficial accounts of the scale of the disaster in Tibet. Photograph: Tingshu Wang/Pool Reuters/AP

“The government needs journalists to uncover uncomfortable truths because it needs accurate information in order to govern effectively,” they say. “But if journalists are given completely free rein to uncover and publish those truths, they may expose things that are politically uncomfortable or challenge the interests of the state.”

Bandurski says: “The [Communist] party sees itself in a global public-opinion struggle. It is wrestling with the world fighting to get its view out. This is how China sees information globally, in a very, very oppositional framework.”

Phuntsok hopes his family on the Nepal side could still be alive. His grandfather, Wangyal, uncle Janngchup, aunt Sumchok and their young child Yeshi Dorjee are still missing.

On the Tibet side he is unwilling to share the names of his missing relatives with the Guardian for security reasons.

Kalsang Jigme, a Tibetan journalist based in New Delhi, says: “Normally, when there’s some disaster, people are very active, praying and support, and they send goods to the affected area. But this time they’re completely silenced.”

बाढ़ केरऽ आपदा चीनी अधिकारियऽ द्वारा “स्वच्छ इंटरनेट २०२६” केरऽ बढ़तऽ उपयोग के उदाहरण छेकै, जे लोक सुरक्षा मंत्रालय केरऽ एगो लंबा समय स॑ चलै वाला अभियान केरऽ नवीनतम संस्करण छेकै जेकरा म॑ अधिकारियऽ द्वारा गलत जानकारी के रूप म॑ जे भी चीज मानलऽ जाय छै ओकरा अपराधी ठहराबै छै, जेकरा म॑ बाढ़ केरऽ अनौपचारिक विवरण भी शामिल छै ।

ई एगो सुस्थापित प्लेबुक के अनुसरण करै छै, जेकरा म॑ अधिकारियऽ आधिकारिक कथ्य क॑ बढ़ावा दै छै, स्वतंत्र खाता क॑ दबाबै छै, आपदा के कारणऽ क॑ वापस देखै के प्रयास क॑ हतोत्साहित करै छै आरू सरकार द्वारा मंजूर कथ्य स॑ अलग दावा पोस्ट करै वाला क॑ सजा दै छै ।

जहाँ ई अभियान केरऽ पहलऽ संस्करण साइबर अपराध आरू हैकिंग प॑ केंद्रित छेलै, वहीं एकरऽ इस्तेमाल तेजी स॑ ओकरा निशाना बनाबै लेली करलऽ जाय रहलऽ छै जेकरा अधिकारियऽ न॑ “अफवाह” कहै छै जेकरा म॑ आपदा के बारे म॑ अनौपचारिक जानकारी भी शामिल छै ।

अमेरिका स्थित तिब्बती वकालत समूह इंटरनेशनल कैंपेन फॉर तिब्बत केरऽ टेंचो ग्यात्सो न॑ कहलकै कि ई अभियान दोहरी उद्देश्य के पूरा करै छै ।धोखाधड़ी आरू गलत सूचना जैसनऽ वास्तविक समस्या स॑ निपटै के साथ-साथ सार्वजनिक कथ्य प॑ नियंत्रण कड़ा करना । “ओह दोहरी उद्देश्य अछि जे आलोचना करब बेसी सूक्ष्म आ चुनौतीपूर्ण बना दैत अछि।”

बाढ़ के बाद के घंटों में शोधकर्ता के कहनाय छनि जे चीनी सोशल मीडिया पर हुनका रुचि में भारी उछाल देखल गेल. विषय ट्रेंड छल, मुदा फेर रियल टाइम मे कमेंट हटाओल गेलाक कारणे खसि पड़ल।

फुलस्क्रीन में छवि देखू ग्यिरॉंग बंदरगाह पर आपदा सं प्रभावित इलाका में श्रद्धांजलि के रूप में फूल के कीचड़ पर राखल गेल अछि. फोटोग्राफ : टिंगशु वांग/पूल रायटर/एपी

गार्जियन द्वारा देखल गेल स्क्रीनशॉट मे चीनी ऐप वीचैट बाढ़ के बारे मे पोस्ट पर रोक लगा रहल अछि. एक मामला म॑ वीचैट द्वारा एगो यूजर क॑ सूचित करलऽ गेलै कि बाढ़ के बारे म॑ एगो पोस्ट के रिपोर्ट करलऽ गेलऽ छै आरू ओकरा बाद “राजनीतिक रूप स॑ संवेदनशील सामग्री” के कारण डिलीट करी देलऽ गेलऽ छै । एकटा आओर के शेयर करय सं रोकल गेल. कहलऽ गेलऽ छेलै कि ई “नीति के उल्लंघन के कारण अनुपलब्ध” छै आरू एकरा म॑ “निषिद्ध सामग्री” छै ।

चीनी मीडिया के निगरानी करै वाला शोध समूह चाइना मीडिया प्रोजेक्ट के निदेशक डेविड बांडर्स्की कहै छै, “[ट्रेंड] लगातार बदलत॑ जाय रहलऽ छेलै आरू ओकरा म॑ हेरफेर करलऽ जाय रहलऽ छेलै, कैन्हेंकि वास्तविक रुचि छेलै । “‘दमन’ सही शब्द नै छै, कैन्हेंकि वू दमन नै करै छै. ई जन-मत के मार्गदर्शन के नीति के लगातार, लगातार, रोजमर्रा के अनुप्रयोग छै।”

आपदा के चारि दिन बाद 30 अगस्त क॑ तिब्बत केरऽ पुलिस न॑ स्वच्छ इंटरनेट २०२६ अभियान के तहत आपदा के बारे म॑ “अफवाह” स॑ जुड़लऽ १० मामला के रिपोर्ट करलकै । अधिकांश मामला मे दावा कैल गेल जे बाढ़ि मे एक हजार स बेसी लोक बह गेल अछि। एखन धरि चीनी अधिकारी 43 गोटेक मृत्युक संख्या जारी कएने छथि ।मानव अधिकार आ तिब्बती वकालत समूह चीन सरकार पर आरोप लगौने अछि जे ओ मृतकक असली पैमाना नुका रहल अछि ।

पुलिस नोटिस म॑ कहलऽ गेलऽ छेलै कि “अफवाह” फैलाबै स॑ “जनता क॑ गुमराह करलऽ जाय छै आरू ऑनलाइन ऑर्डर म॑ बाधा पहुँचै छै” आरू एकरऽ उद्देश्य छेलै कि “आपदा राहत के काम सुचारू रूप स॑ आगू बढ़ैलऽ जाय” ।

आपदा स॑ ३,००० किलोमीटर दूर प्रांत जियांगसी केरऽ एगो यूजर न॑ वीडियो प्लेटफॉर्म प॑ पोस्ट करी क॑ दावा करलकै कि “लापता लोगऽ के संख्या बढ़ी क॑ ८२६ होय गेलऽ छै” । पुलिस रिपोर्ट के अनुसार उपयोगकर्ता क॑ “प्रशासनिक दंड” के सामना करना पड़लै, बिना ई निर्दिष्ट करलऽ कि ओकरा म॑ की शामिल छै ।

‘राज्य मेहनत क’ रहल अछि से साबित करब’।

चीन केरऽ एगो पूर्व सरकारी मीडिया पत्रकार, जे प्रतिशोध के डर स॑ नाम नै बताबै के शर्त प॑ बोलै लेली राजी होय गेलऽ छेलै, के कहना छै कि संकट के समय म॑ नियंत्रण भी जानकारी के साधारण चूक के माध्यम स॑ काम करै छै जेतना कि दमन के माध्यम स॑ : “आधिकारिक समाचार कवरेज ई साबित करै लेली भारी जगह दै छै कि राज्य मेहनत करी रहलऽ छै, लेकिन सबसें बुनियादी सवालऽ के जवाब दै म॑ बहुत कम जानकारी दै छै कि के गायब छै? आखिरी बार ओकरा कहाँ देखलऽ गेलऽ छेलै? खोजल गेल?

“नियंत्रण बहुत सख्त भ गेल अछि, खास क इंटरनेट क संबंध मे, हालांकि एहि मे बारीकियों अछि, किया कि एखनो प्रतिबंध कए बाईपास करबाक तरीका अछि। जेना कि जल्दी सं पोस्ट क या सामग्री के माध्यम सं पहुंचाबय लेल पर्दाफाश भाषा के प्रयोग क' क'.'

लेकिन कुछ रिपोर्टिंग के अनुमति देला स॑ केंद्रीय अधिकारियऽ के हित के काम होय सकै छै, ई बात के कहना छै कि कोविड महामारी के दौरान प्रसारक म॑ काम करै वाला एगो पूर्व संपादक आरू जे प्रतिशोध के डर स॑ नाम नै बताबै लेली भी कहलकै ।

हुनकऽ कहना छै कि सरकार क॑ असहज सच्चाई के खुलासा करै लेली पत्रकारऽ के जरूरत छै, कैन्हेंकि ओकरा प्रभावी ढंग स॑ शासन करै लेली सही जानकारी के जरूरत छै । “मुदा पत्रकारऽ क॑ अगर वू सच्चाई क॑ उजागर करै आरू प्रकाशित करै के पूरा तरह स॑ आजादी देलऽ जाय त॑ वू राजनीतिक रूप स॑ असहज होय वाला बात क॑ उजागर करी सकै छै या राज्य केरऽ हित क॑ चुनौती द॑ सकै छै ।”

बांदुर्स्की कहै छै: "[कम्युनिस्ट] पार्टी खुद क॑ वैश्विक जन-मत संघर्ष म॑ देखै छै । ई अपनऽ विचार क॑ बाहर निकालै लेली लड़ै वाला दुनिया के साथ कुश्ती करी रहलऽ छै । चीन वैश्विक स्तर प॑ जानकारी क॑ ई तरह स॑ देखै छै, बहुत, बहुत विपक्षी ढाँचा म॑।"

फुंत्सोक के आशा छै कि नेपाल तरफ के हुनकऽ परिवार अखनी भी जीवित रह॑ सकै छै । हुनकऽ दादा वांगयाल, चाचा जंगचुप, चाची सुमचोक आरू हुनकऽ छोटऽ बच्चा येशी दोर्जी अखनी भी लापता छै ।

तिब्बत पक्ष स॑ हुनी सुरक्षा कारण स॑ अपनऽ लापता रिश्तेदारऽ के नाम गार्जियन के साथ साझा करै लेली तैयार नै छै ।

नई दिल्ली स्थित तिब्बती पत्रकार कलसांग जिग्मे कहैत छथि: "सामान्य तौर पर जखन कोनो आपदा अबैत अछि त’ लोक बहुत सक्रिय रहैत छथि, प्रार्थना आ समर्थन करैत छथि, आ ओ प्रभावित इलाका मे सामान पठा दैत छथि. मुदा एहि बेर हुनका पूरा तरहे चुप क’ देल जाइत छनि."

title: One year on from Nepal protests, have Gen Z demands been met? - Al Jazeera
description: One year on from Nepal protests, have Gen Z demands been met?  Al Jazeera
publisher.title: Al Jazeera
full_article:
One year ago, thousands of young people took to the streets in multiple Nepali cities to protest against corruption. Following the resulting curfews, arrests and the killing of protesters in a crackdown on the demonstrations, the Gen Z‑led movement forced the government from power, ushering in an interim administration and opening the way for new elections.

Now, as Nepal grapples with the aftermath of devastating floods along its border with Tibet, we examine what has changed over the past year – and whether the demands of the Gen Z protesters have been met.

What happened in Nepal last year?

On September 8, 2025, youth-led “Gen Z” protests began in Kathmandu and other cities of Nepal.

Demonstrators who took to the streets were protesting a series of corruption scandals in the country and were also angered by the rising trend of the children of Nepali government officials – dubbed “Nepo kids” – documenting their lavish lifestyles online.

The protests broke out just days after the country blocked 26 social media sites including Facebook, Instagram, X (formerly Twitter), and TikTok for not complying with government rules about “harmful” content. This ban was lifted when the protests began.

Some young demonstrators defied curfews imposed by the authorities after demonstrations began, leading to arrests and the police firing live rounds at protesters, killing about 76 people. Hundreds of protesters were injured and hundreds more arrested. Protesters also set fire to several government buildings, including parliament, and the army was deployed.

Advertisement

Then, on September 9, Prime Minister KP Oli, 74, resigned from his position. Within a week, Nepal’s former Chief Justice Sushila Karki had been appointed as the country’s new interim prime minister.

Ultimately, the protests culminated in the current government being formed in March this year when 35-year-old rapper-turned-politician Balendra Shah was sworn in as the country’s youngest-ever prime minister.

Shah leads the Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP), also known as the National Independent Party, a new anti‑establishment party which emerged after the youth-led protests and won more than two‑thirds of the 165 directly elected seats in parliament in March. Traditional parties such as the Nepali Congress and the CPN‑UML have a much smaller representation than ever before.

Although he was not a street organiser of the protests, Shah became one of the most prominent political figures, channelling Gen Z’s anger into his electoral campaign.

What were the key demands of the Gen Z protesters?

They included:

An end to corruption: Protesters demanded greater transparency and accountability from political elites they view as corrupt, as well as an end to nepotism, whereby the children of those elites live in luxury while many young Nepalis struggle financially.

Protesters demanded greater transparency and accountability from political elites they view as corrupt, as well as an end to nepotism, whereby the children of those elites live in luxury while many young Nepalis struggle financially. Mass resignations and suspensions: Protesters called for the resignation of Prime Minister KP Sharma Oli and the mass resignation of parliamentarians. They also called for an immediate suspension of officials who issued the order to fire on protesters.

Protesters called for the resignation of Prime Minister KP Sharma Oli and the mass resignation of parliamentarians. They also called for an immediate suspension of officials who issued the order to fire on protesters. Political overhaul: The protesters called for the dissolution of parliament, establishment of an interim government and holding new general elections.

Have these demands been met?

The demands have been met to some extent.

For instance, Oli resigned in the wake of the Gen Z‑led protests, and several senior members of his government also stepped down. Parliament was dissolved, an interim government was established, and new general elections were held in March this year.

“Despite the loss of life and property during the movement, the interim government successfully conducted peaceful elections, leading to the emergence of a new political force in government,” Yog Raj Lamichhane, an assistant professor at Nepal’s Pokhara University, told Al Jazeera.

“The result reflected public disenchantment with the old political establishment.”

In March this year, Nepal police arrested Oli and former Home Affairs Minister Ramesh Lekhak for their alleged involvement in the deadly crackdown on the protesters last year.

Advertisement

However, both men were released in April after a Supreme Court order asked the police not to indefinitely extend the detention. They remain under investigation in connection with last year’s deadly Gen Z protests, but have not been formally charged.

Furthermore, the issue of corruption among political elites has barely been addressed, observers say.

Dinesh Paudel, professor at the Appalachain State University in the US, told Al Jazeera: “The fundamental concerns and issues raised by the young protestor last year are still the same, and there are no governance style changes even after the new elected government, other than some populist rhetorics on small and cosmetic topics.”

Has the leadership change made any difference?

Some of the young leaders have entered parliament and government, while others remain in activist groups. The divisions between these two groups of people are becoming more apparent as they often clash over how much to compromise with the old political establishment.

Those who were elected to parliament in March mostly belong to the Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP), or National Independent Party.

“One of the most exciting and progressive parts is the emergence of youth in politics as most of the parliamentarians are young, educated and have much aspiration to change,” Bishnu Raj Upreti, a public policy analyst and research director at Nepal Centre for Contemporary Research (NCCR), told Al Jazeera.

“The leadership change appears to have brought some positive differences, particularly in the working style of the current prime minister,” Lamichhane said.

However, experts say the younger generation of MPs – those elected under the NIP/RSP banner as well as those in older parties – remains constrained by party hierarchies and Nepal’s entrenched political system.

“They are inexperienced and are still heavily controlled by party structures,” Upreti said. He added that wider generational distrust between young politicians and the older establishment also complicated reform efforts.

“Leadership change has started. It is good, but not enough.”

This has resulted in an apparent divide between those in government positions and those in activist groups.

In May this year, the new government invited Gen Z activists – mostly civil society leaders and youth activists – to give their input for constitutional amendments. However, 25 of the 29 invited boycotted the meeting, saying deeper systemic problems and earlier agreements with the previous administration were being ignored, according to Gen Z activist Aayush Basyal.

Basyal, who was present at the protests last year, said it was “really tricky” for young activists to adjust to working inside the system alongside the new Gen‑Z politicians now in office. “They are trying to cooperate with the authorities they previously challenged, while still pushing for the radical changes they demanded on the streets,” she explained.

“Now the Gen Z protesters of that time are divided into different factions, and some of the factions are vehemently opposing some work of government,” Upreti explained.

Advertisement

“So those who oppose the government are not in positive booking of the government,” Upreti added.

Where are the protesters now?

On Tuesday, families of protesters who were killed in last year’s crackdown organised a formal commemoration at what used to be Nepal’s parliament building.

After functioning as the parliament building for almost two decades, it shut down last year when Gen Z protesters trespassed and set fire to it.

Basyal said the authorities provided tight security amid rumours that some groups might try to incite violence, noting that Nepal’s “media economy” often amplifies sensational incidents even when only a few people are involved.

In the meantime, however, the divide within the Gen Z movement is becoming more stark, particularly what some see as a failure by the new leaders to advocate for protesters.

“The injured protesters have generally received medical treatment and certain monetary compensation,” Lamicchane said.

“However, the concept of compensation remains broader than financial support alone. In my view, the true compensation would be the fulfilment of the promises and objectives that inspired the Gen Z movement and the subsequent formation of a new government.”

Basyal said that while some of the people involved in the movement are now MPs or cabinet ministers, others, from poor, minority backgrounds, who lack money and influence, are still in jail and cannot speak up for themselves.

“There are people still in jail, officially more than 900 and unofficially, maybe like 1,600 plus, who are in jail for arson,” Basyal said.

He said it was troubling that these protesters remain in jail, suggesting this risks becoming “institutionalised” and raising questions over whether the government is effectively celebrating impunity.

Activists, he added, hope the new administration will treat these detainees better, but “that is yet to be seen.”

What still needs to change?

Analysts say structural changes are necessary.

“Although the government has promised reforms, particularly through changes in laws and policies, these commitments have not yet been substantially realised,” Lamichhane said.

Upreti noted that the new government has not begun any structural changes at all.

“Structural changes have to start with changing existing laws and bringing in new laws and policies,” he said.

“From what we’ve seen so far, the new leaders don’t appear to be prioritising that. Massive reform of the bureaucracy is a precondition to achieving the aims of the Gen Z movement, but the government has not yet done meaningful work in this line.”

He added that another important element is to develop better relations and deeper trust with Nepal’s two giant neighbours, India and China, since Nepal’s economic progress and geopolitical balance depend on them.

Experts also say Nepal’s highly centralised system of government is a major obstacle to deeper structural reform.

“Strong collaboration of the federal movement with provincial and local government is the necessary condition for advancing economic progress, but they ignore provincial and local government as they have no provincial and local government. It is not a good approach,” Upreti said.

“Structural changes are necessary and they come from internal power dynamics such as urban-rural divide, inherent conflict between educated elites and peasant farmers and economic and bureaucratically institutionalised corruption,” Paudel said. “It is hard to imagine that there will be any structural changes, aiming to making people’s lives better, at this stage and under current circumstances.

Advertisement

“In short, Nepal has missed yet another opportunity from a popular uprising that would fundamentally address Nepali peoples desire for change.”

What’s next?

“This new government seems to be deeply under its own weight of expectation,” Basyal said.

He explained that historically in Nepal, there’s been an “expectation gap”: people expect a lot, governments deliver little, and that gap fuels frustration.

He said that this government has “not been transparent”.

“The prime minister, he doesn’t speak a lot in the parliament. And when he did address the parliament a few times, that was pretty chaotic, as well,” Basyal added.

“If this issue remains unaddressed, it may lead to a second wave of public disenchantment.”

Lamichhane said, however, it will take time to see if the government can address the challenges it faces.

“Let’s hope and wait for changes. Now, it’s not the appropriate time to criticise the government, as Nepal has faced an apocalypse in the form of a massive flood.”

Meanwhile, flags in Nepal flew at half-mast on Monday as the country mourned the more-than-1,300 people who are known to have died in catastrophic floods which ravaged the border region with Tibet late last month. Thousands more people are still missing.

Basyal noted that Nepal’s current constitution was finalised and promulgated in September 2015, only after the devastating April and May earthquakes created urgent political pressure to end nearly a decade of deadlock.

“It feels like the nation comes together only during national disasters. So we’re really hopeful that this sense of unity that is right now will help.”
